Risk Category: HIGH
Corrective Action: Relocate screening plant or fine material heaps outside 80m buffer zone
Violation Condition: Placing coal screening plant or fine material heaps within 80m of intake shaft top
Project Relevance: HIGH
Relevance Reason: Siting requirement to prevent surface dust from polluting underground air.

regulation_title: Inspection and testing of dust control devices and respirators
rag_text:
Regulation Number: 143
Regulation Title: Inspection and testing of dust control devices and respirators
Chapter: XI
Clause Number: other
Requirement Type: inspection
Requirement: Every device used for prevention/suppression of dust, air filtering, and every dust respirator shall be inspected once at least every 7 days, thoroughly examined and tested monthly, and recorded in the dust register.
Responsible Role: Dust In-charge, Competent Person
Responsible Entity: Mine Management/Owner
Applicability: All dust suppression systems and respirators
Trigger Event: Weekly inspection and monthly testing cycle
Frequency: weekly
Deadline: not_specified
Reporting Required: False
Reporting Method: not_specified
Reporting Authority: not_specified
Document Required: Not specified
Record Required: Dust control device inspection and test register
Required Evidence: Signed weekly inspection and monthly test records
Inspection Required: Yes
Inspection Frequency: Every 7 days inspection / monthly test
Equipment Requirement: Dust suppression devices, filters, respirators
Hazard: Equipment failure leading to uncontrolled dust exposure
Risk Category: HIGH
Corrective Action: Inspect, repair, or replace defective dust prevention devices and respirators
Violation Condition: Failure to inspect dust devices weekly or test monthly
Project Relevance: HIGH
Relevance Reason: Routine maintenance and inspection schedule for compliance safety.

regulation_title: Manager's scheme for dust sampling and control
rag_text:
Regulation Number: 143
Regulation Title: Manager's scheme for dust sampling and control
Chapter: XI
Clause Number: other
Requirement Type: document
Requirement: The manager of every mine generating airborne dust shall formulate and implement a scheme specifying sampling location/frequency, instruments, testing lab, recording formats, monitoring organization, and worker instruction.
Responsible Role: Manager
Responsible Entity: Mine Management/Owner
Applicability: Every mine generating airborne dust
Trigger Event: Generation of airborne dust
Frequency: continuous
Deadline: not_specified
Reporting Required: True
Reporting Method: other
Reporting Authority: regional_inspector
Document Required: Manager's Dust Control and Sampling Scheme
Record Required: Dust Scheme Document
Required Evidence: Formulated, signed, and implemented Manager's Dust Scheme document
Inspection Required: Yes
Inspection Frequency: Periodic regulatory review
Equipment Requirement: Not specified
Hazard: Unsystematic dust control and uncoordinated monitoring
Risk Category: HIGH
Corrective Action: Formulate and implement written dust control scheme immediately
Violation Condition: Operating without a formulated manager's dust scheme
Project Relevance: HIGH
Relevance Reason: Mandatory governance document for mine dust management.

Regulation Number: 144
Regulation Title: Maintenance of dust plan
Chapter: XI
Clause Number: other
Requirement Type: document
Requirement: Every belowground mine shall maintain a dust plan on a scale having representative factor of not less than 2000:1 showing naturally wet areas and areas requiring treatment with water or incombustible dust.
Responsible Role: Manager, Ventilation Officer
Responsible Entity: Mine Management/Owner
Applicability: All belowground mines
Trigger Event: Belowground mining operations
Frequency: continuous
Deadline: not_specified
Reporting Required: False
Reporting Method: not_specified
Reporting Authority: not_specified
Document Required: Dust Plan (RF >= 2000:1)
Record Required: Dust Plan showing color-coded/numbered treatment zones
Required Evidence: Updated Dust Plan on 2000:1 scale with analysis-based treatment intervals
Inspection Required: Yes
Inspection Frequency: Periodic inspection
Equipment Requirement: Not specified
Hazard: Uncontrolled coal dust explosion propagation
Risk Category: HIGH
Corrective Action: Prepare and maintain updated dust plan on scale 2000:1
Violation Condition: Absence of dust plan or RF scale smaller than 2000:1
Project Relevance: HIGH
Relevance Reason: Statutory mapping requirement for coal dust explosion prevention.

regulation_title: Treatment of underground mine workings with incombustible dust or water
rag_text:
Regulation Number: 144
Regulation Title: Treatment of underground mine workings with incombustible dust or water
Chapter: XI
Clause Number: other
Requirement Type: safety
Requirement: Every non-naturally wet part of a mine shall be treated with fine incombustible dust (ensuring >=75% incombustible matter for seam <30% VM, and >=85% for seam >30% VM) or treated with water (ensuring >=30% water by weight).
Responsible Role: Dust In-charge, Manager
Responsible Entity: Mine Management/Owner
Applicability: All belowground workings not naturally wet or unisolated
Trigger Event: Daily mining activity in non-wet areas
Frequency: continuous
Deadline: not_specified
Reporting Required: False
Reporting Method: not_specified
Reporting Authority: not_specified
Document Required: Not specified
Record Required: Daily dust treatment record book
Required Evidence: Dust sample analysis showing >=75% or >=85% incombustible content, or >=30% moisture
Inspection Required: Yes
Inspection Frequency: Daily supervision
Equipment Requirement: Incombustible stone dust, water spraying pipes/drenching system
Hazard: Coal dust explosion
Risk Category: CRITICAL
Corrective Action: Apply stone dust or water to meet required incombustible/moisture percentage
Violation Condition: Incombustible matter content below 75%/85% or moisture below 30% in mine dust
Project Relevance: HIGH
Relevance Reason: Primary technical defense threshold against underground coal dust explosions.

Regulation Number: 144
Regulation Title: Testing of incombustible dust quality
Chapter: XI
Clause Number: other
Requirement Type: inspection
Requirement: Incombustible dust shall be tested at least once every 3 months (or whenever a fresh supply is received from a non-regular source) to ensure silica <= 5%, proper fineness, light color, and dispersibility.
Responsible Role: Manager, Dust In-charge
Responsible Entity: Mine Management/Owner
Applicability: Incombustible dust used in mine treatment
Trigger Event: Quarterly test or receipt of fresh non-regular supply
Frequency: quarterly
Deadline: not_specified
Reporting Required: False
Reporting Method: not_specified
Reporting Authority: not_specified
Document Required: Incombustible dust test report
Record Required: Register of stone dust quality analysis
Required Evidence: Test certificate showing free silica <= 5% and dispersibility compliance
Inspection Required: Yes
Inspection Frequency: Quarterly / per batch
Equipment Requirement: Incombustible dust testing kit
Hazard: Ineffective stone dust failing to suppress explosion or causing silicosis
Risk Category: HIGH
Corrective Action: Discontinue use of non-compliant stone dust batch
Violation Condition: Using stone dust with >5% silica or failing to test stone dust quarterly
Project Relevance: HIGH
Relevance Reason: Quality assurance standard for stone dust safety material.

regulation_title: Appointment and qualification of Dust In-charge
rag_text:
Regulation Number: 144
Regulation Title: Appointment and qualification of Dust In-charge
Chapter: XI
Clause Number: other
Requirement Type: qualification
Requirement: Dust control measures shall be carried out under the supervision of a competent person holding Manager's or Overman's certificate or degree/diploma in mining engineering, designated as 'Dust In-charge'.
Responsible Role: Manager, Dust In-charge
Responsible Entity: Mine Management/Owner
Applicability: All mines requiring dust control
Trigger Event: Appointment of safety supervisory staff
Frequency: continuous
Deadline: not_specified
Reporting Required: False
Reporting Method: not_specified
Reporting Authority: not_specified
Document Required: Appointment letter and qualification certificates
Record Required: Register of statutory appointments
Required Evidence: Manager's/Overman's Certificate or Mining Degree/Diploma
Inspection Required: Yes
Inspection Frequency: Periodic statutory audit
Equipment Requirement: Not specified
Hazard: Inadequate dust control due to unqualified supervision
Risk Category: MEDIUM
Corrective Action: Appoint qualified Dust In-charge holding statutory certificate
Violation Condition: Designating an unqualified person as Dust In-charge
Project Relevance: HIGH
Relevance Reason: Statutory staffing requirement for mine compliance.

regulation_title: Restriction on duties of Dust In-charge
rag_text:
Regulation Number: 144
Regulation Title: Restriction on duties of Dust In-charge
Chapter: XI
Clause Number: other
Requirement Type: governance
Requirement: No duties with respect to sampling of dust under regulation 145 or any other duties shall be entrusted to the Dust In-charge without previous written permission of Regional Inspector (except mines with output <5000 tonnes/month).
Responsible Role: Manager, Dust In-charge
Responsible Entity: Mine Management/Owner
Applicability: Mines with monthly output >= 5000 tonnes
Trigger Event: Assignment of duties to Dust In-charge
Frequency: continuous
Deadline: not_specified
Reporting Required: True
Reporting Method: application_or_approval
Reporting Authority: regional_inspector
Document Required: Written permission from Regional Inspector if dual duties assigned
Record Required: Duty assignment register
Required Evidence: Written permission from RI or proof of mine output <5000 tonnes
Inspection Required: Yes
Inspection Frequency: Periodic audit
Equipment Requirement: Not specified
Hazard: Conflict of interest / oversight failure in dust treatment sampling
Risk Category: MEDIUM
Corrective Action: Separate Dust In-charge and Sampling In-charge duties
Violation Condition: Assigning dust sampling duties to Dust In-charge without RI permission in mine output >=5000 t/month
Project Relevance: HIGH
Relevance Reason: Segregation of duties rule for compliance integrity.

regulation_title: Zoning of roadways for dust sampling
rag_text:
Regulation Number: 145
Regulation Title: Zoning of roadways for dust sampling
Chapter: XI
Clause Number: other
Requirement Type: compliance
Requirement: Every return airway within 200m of last working face and every non-naturally wet haulage/tramming/conveyor roadway shall be divided into zones not longer than 150 meters each.
Responsible Role: Sampling Incharge, Manager
Responsible Entity: Mine Management/Owner
Applicability: Belowground return airways and transport roadways
Trigger Event: Mine layout development and sampling plan creation
Frequency: continuous
Deadline: not_specified
Reporting Required: False
Reporting Method: not_specified
Reporting Authority: not_specified
Document Required: Sampling Plan (scale >= 2000:1)
Record Required: Zone demarcation register and sampling plan
Required Evidence: Zones <= 150m marked on sampling plan and underground notice boards
Inspection Required: Yes
Inspection Frequency: Periodic verification
Equipment Requirement: Zone notice boards underground
Hazard: Unsystematic dust monitoring missing high-risk coal dust buildup
Risk Category: MEDIUM
Corrective Action: Divide roadways into zones not exceeding 150 meters and mark on plan
Violation Condition: Zones exceeding 150 meters length or un-demarcated roadways
Project Relevance: HIGH
Relevance Reason: Spatial sampling framework standard for mine dust audit.

regulation_title: Frequency of representative mine dust sampling
rag_text:
Regulation Number: 145
Regulation Title: Frequency of representative mine dust sampling
Chapter: XI
Clause Number: other
Requirement Type: monitoring
Requirement: Representative samples of dust shall be collected once in every thirty days from every zone, rotating through sections a, b, or c so that all sections are sampled.
Responsible Role: Sampling Incharge
Responsible Entity: Mine Management/Owner
Applicability: All designated mine dust sampling zones
Trigger Event: 30-day sampling cycle
Frequency: monthly
Deadline: not_specified
Reporting Required: False
Reporting Method: not_specified
Reporting Authority: not_specified
Document Required: Not specified
Record Required: Dust sample collection logbook
Required Evidence: Dust sample test reports for every zone recorded every 30 days
Inspection Required: Yes
Inspection Frequency: Monthly
Equipment Requirement: Not specified
Hazard: Undetected explosive coal dust accumulation
Risk Category: HIGH
Corrective Action: Collect representative dust samples across all sections within 30 days
Violation Condition: Failure to collect dust samples from any zone within 30 days
Project Relevance: HIGH
Relevance Reason: Mandatory periodic sampling cycle for underground explosion control.

regulation_title: Supervision and recording of sampling results
rag_text:
Regulation Number: 145
Regulation Title: Supervision and recording of sampling results
Chapter: XI
Clause Number: multiple_clauses
Requirement Type: record
Requirement: Sampling operations shall be supervised by a Sampling Incharge holding Manager's/Overman's Certificate or Mining Degree/Diploma. Analysis results sent within 7 days shall be recorded immediately in a bound paged book signed by Sampling Incharge and countersigned by Manager.
Responsible Role: Sampling Incharge, Manager
Responsible Entity: Mine Management/Owner
Applicability: Mine dust sampling and analysis
Trigger Event: Sample collection and analysis receipt
Frequency: weekly
Deadline: immediate
Reporting Required: False
Reporting Method: not_specified
Reporting Authority: not_specified
Document Required: Bound-paged Sampling Analysis Register
Record Required: Analysis result entries signed by Sampling Incharge and countersigned by Manager
Required Evidence: Signed and dated entries in bound-paged sampling register
Inspection Required: Yes
Inspection Frequency: Periodic regulatory audit
Equipment Requirement: Not specified
Hazard: Unqualified sampling or undocumented dust explosion hazards
Risk Category: HIGH
Corrective Action: Send samples for analysis within 7 days and record signed results
Violation Condition: Delaying sample analysis dispatch beyond 7 days or missing Manager countersignature
Project Relevance: HIGH
Relevance Reason: Statutory audit trail and governance for coal dust analysis.

Regulation Number: 146
Regulation Title: Stone dust barriers
Chapter: XI
Clause Number: multiple_clauses
Requirement Type: safety
Requirement: In every gassy seam of 2nd or 3rd degree or 1st degree development with inflammable gas likelihood, stone dust barriers approved by Chief Inspector shall be provided to prevent explosion propagation.
Responsible Role: Manager, Owner, Agent
Responsible Entity: Mine Management/Owner
Applicability: 2nd/3rd degree gassy seams and 1st degree gassy development workings
Trigger Event: Mine development in gassy seams
Frequency: continuous
Deadline: not_specified
Reporting Required: True
Reporting Method: application_or_approval
Reporting Authority: chief_inspector
Document Required: Chief Inspector's approval for stone dust barrier design
Record Required: Stone dust barrier maintenance register
Required Evidence: Installed approved stone dust barriers maintained in designated workings
Inspection Required: Yes
Inspection Frequency: Weekly inspection
Equipment Requirement: Approved stone dust barrier system
Hazard: Coal dust / firedamp explosion propagation across mine districts
Risk Category: CRITICAL
Corrective Action: Install approved stone dust barriers in designated gassy seam workings
Violation Condition: Absence of approved stone dust barriers in 2nd/3rd degree gassy seams
Project Relevance: HIGH
Relevance Reason: Major explosion prevention control requirement.

Regulation Number: 147
Regulation Title: Precautions against eruption of gas
Chapter: XI
Clause Number: other
Requirement Type: safety
Requirement: Where any working is extended to within 30 meters of any goaf or disused working likely to contain inflammable/noxious gases, at least one bore-hole >= 1.5m deep shall be maintained in advance under competent person supervision, using only approved safety lamps.
Responsible Role: Manager, Competent Person
Responsible Entity: Mine Management/Owner
Applicability: Workings approaching within 30m of disused workings or goaf
Trigger Event: Working approaching within 30 meters of goaf/disused workings
Frequency: continuous
Deadline: not_specified
Reporting Required: False
Reporting Method: not_specified
Reporting Authority: not_specified
Document Required: Not specified
Record Required: Advance borehole drilling record logbook
Required Evidence: Boreholes >= 1.5m deep maintained ahead of face and competent person supervision logs
Inspection Required: Yes
Inspection Frequency: Daily during advance
Equipment Requirement: Drilling equipment for 1.5m boreholes, approved safety lamps
Hazard: Gas outburst / toxic gas eruption from abandoned workings
Risk Category: CRITICAL
Corrective Action: Maintain advance boreholes of >= 1.5m under competent supervision
Violation Condition: Working within 30m of goaf without advance 1.5m boreholes or using unapproved lights
Project Relevance: HIGH
Relevance Reason: Critical safety protocol against underground gas outburst.

regulation_title: Notice for reopening isolated, sealed or flooded workings
rag_text:
Regulation Number: 148
Regulation Title: Notice for reopening isolated, sealed or flooded workings
Chapter: XI
Clause Number: other
Requirement Type: reporting
Requirement: Owner, agent or manager shall give written notice of intention to reopen a mine/part isolated, sealed or flooded to deal with fire/heating at least 30 days before starting work to Regional Inspector and Chief Inspector.
Responsible Role: Owner, Agent, Manager
Responsible Entity: Mine Management/Owner
Applicability: Reopening of sealed/flooded fire areas
Trigger Event: Proposal to reopen sealed/flooded mine area
Frequency: pre_operation
Deadline: before_event
Reporting Required: True
Reporting Method: written_notification
Reporting Authority: chief_and_regional_inspector
Document Required: Written Notice of Reopening
Record Required: Copy of reopening notice and acknowledgment receipt
Required Evidence: Written notice submitted 30 days prior to starting reopening operations
Inspection Required: Yes
Inspection Frequency: Prior to reopening permission
Equipment Requirement: Not specified
Hazard: Re-ignition of fire, toxic gas blowout upon reopening
Risk Category: HIGH
Corrective Action: Submit 30-day prior written notice to authorities before commencing work
Violation Condition: Commencing reopening of sealed fire area without giving 30 days written notice
Project Relevance: HIGH
Relevance Reason: Statutory prior notice requirement for reopening hazardous mine areas.

Regulation Number: 148
Regulation Title: Exploratory work in irrespirable atmosphere
Chapter: XI
Clause Number: other
Requirement Type: emergency
Requirement: Exploratory work in irrespirable atmosphere shall be done under rescue cover only, by a party of not less than 3 persons carrying approved CO detector and flame safety lamp.
Responsible Role: Manager, Rescue Team Leader
Responsible Entity: Mine Management/Owner
Applicability: Exploratory work in irrespirable mine atmosphere
Trigger Event: Exploratory entry into irrespirable atmosphere
Frequency: other
Deadline: not_specified
Reporting Required: False
Reporting Method: not_specified
Reporting Authority: not_specified
Document Required: Rescue operation plan / log
Record Required: Rescue team entry register and gas test logs
Required Evidence: Rescue cover deployment, min 3 team members, equipped with CO detector and flame safety lamp
Inspection Required: Yes
Inspection Frequency: Continuous during operation
Equipment Requirement: Self-contained breathing apparatus (rescue cover), approved CO detector, flame safety lamp
Hazard: Asphyxiation, toxic gas poisoning, explosion
Risk Category: CRITICAL
Corrective Action: Ensure full rescue apparatus cover and team size >= 3 with testing gear
Violation Condition: Sending less than 3 persons or exploring without rescue cover/CO detector into irrespirable air
Project Relevance: HIGH
Relevance Reason: High-risk rescue emergency protocol.

regulation_title: Height of mine entrance above Highest Flood Level (HFL)
rag_text:
Regulation Number: 149
Regulation Title: Height of mine entrance above Highest Flood Level (HFL)
Chapter: XI
Clause Number: other
Requirement Type: safety
Requirement: Every entrance into a mine shall be constructed and maintained so that its lowest point is not less than 1.5 meters above the highest flood level (HFL) at that point, except with written permission of Chief Inspector.
Responsible Role: Manager, Owner, Agent
Responsible Entity: Mine Management/Owner
Applicability: All surface mine entrances (shafts, inclines, adits)
Trigger Event: Design and maintenance of mine entry
Frequency: continuous
Deadline: not_specified
Reporting Required: True
Reporting Method: application_or_approval
Reporting Authority: chief_inspector
Document Required: Chief Inspector written permission (if < 1.5m above HFL)
Record Required: Surveyed HFL record and entrance elevation map
Required Evidence: Survey plan proving entrance elevation >= 1.5m above HFL
Inspection Required: Yes
Inspection Frequency: Annual monsoon check
Equipment Requirement: Not specified
Hazard: Surface water inrush flooding underground mine
Risk Category: CRITICAL
Corrective Action: Raise entrance sill or construct flood protection wall >= 1.5m above HFL
Violation Condition: Mine entrance lowest point less than 1.5m above HFL without written permission
Project Relevance: HIGH
Relevance Reason: Critical inundation safety barrier rule.

regulation_title: Danger level marking and withdrawal of persons during surface flood
rag_text:
Regulation Number: 149
Regulation Title: Danger level marking and withdrawal of persons during surface flood
Chapter: XI
Clause Number: other
Requirement Type: emergency
Requirement: Highest flood level and danger level (at least 1.2m below HFL) shall be permanently marked. Whenever surface water reaches danger level, all persons shall be withdrawn from the mine.
Responsible Role: Manager, Owner, Agent
Responsible Entity: Mine Management/Owner
Applicability: Mines likely to be endangered by surface water
Trigger Event: Surface water level rising towards danger level
Frequency: continuous
Deadline: not_specified
Reporting Required: False
Reporting Method: not_specified
Reporting Authority: not_specified
Document Required: Not specified
Record Required: Monsoon flood monitoring logbook
Required Evidence: Permanent danger level pillars marked and emergency communication system functional
Inspection Required: Yes
Inspection Frequency: Every 14 days during monsoon
Equipment Requirement: Quick communication system to all underground parts
Hazard: Catastrophic mine inundation from surface flooding
Risk Category: CRITICAL
Corrective Action: Withdraw all underground persons immediately when water hits danger level
Violation Condition: Failing to withdraw workers when surface water reaches marked danger level
Project Relevance: HIGH
Relevance Reason: Emergency evacuation trigger for flood hazard monitoring.

regulation_title: Restriction on workings vertically below water bodies or within 15 meters
rag_text:
Regulation Number: 149
Regulation Title: Restriction on workings vertically below water bodies or within 15 meters
Chapter: XI
Clause Number: other
Requirement Type: safety
Requirement: No working shall be made vertically below any river, canal, lake, tank/reservoir, or within 15 meters horizontal distance from banks/boundaries, except with prior written permission of Chief Inspector.
Responsible Role: Manager, Owner, Agent
Responsible Entity: Mine Management/Owner
Applicability: Workings near surface water bodies
Trigger Event: Mine layout planning near surface water body
Frequency: pre_operation
Deadline: not_specified
Reporting Required: True
Reporting Method: application_or_approval
Reporting Authority: chief_inspector
Document Required: Chief Inspector Written Permission and statutory plans
Record Required: Permission letter and boundary surveyed plan
Required Evidence: Written permission from Chief Inspector and horizontal barrier >= 15m
Inspection Required: Yes
Inspection Frequency: Every 14 days in monsoon / 30 days other
Equipment Requirement: Not specified
Hazard: Massive water inrush due to strata collapse under water body
Risk Category: CRITICAL
Corrective Action: Stop working within 15m safety barrier and apply for Chief Inspector permission
Violation Condition: Working vertically below water body or within 15m horizontal distance without written permission
Project Relevance: HIGH
Relevance Reason: High-risk structural safety restriction preventing inundation.

regulation_title: Periodic examination of flood protective measures
rag_text:
Regulation Number: 149
Regulation Title: Periodic examination of flood protective measures
Chapter: XI
Clause Number: multiple_clauses
Requirement Type: inspection
Requirement: A competent person shall examine every flood protective measure once at least every 14 days during rainy season and every 30 days during other periods. Manager shall personally inspect them once at least every quarter.
Responsible Role: Competent Person, Manager
Responsible Entity: Mine Management/Owner
Applicability: All surface flood protection structures
Trigger Event: Routine inspection schedule (seasonal)
Frequency: monthly
Deadline: not_specified
Reporting Required: False
Reporting Method: not_specified
Reporting Authority: not_specified
Document Required: Bound paged examination book
Record Required: Signed and dated protective measure inspection report
Required Evidence: Inspection reports signed by competent person and countersigned by Manager
Inspection Required: Yes
Inspection Frequency: Every 14 days (rainy) / 30 days (other) / Quarterly (Manager)
Equipment Requirement: Not specified
Hazard: Failure of surface flood bunds, dams, or drainage structures
Risk Category: HIGH
Corrective Action: Perform immediate inspection and repair compromised embankment/dams
Violation Condition: Failure to inspect flood protection measures every 14 days during monsoon or quarterly by manager
Project Relevance: HIGH
Relevance Reason: Periodic inspection schedule for surface flood barriers.

regulation_title: Permission for workings approaching within 60 meters of water/liquid accumulation
rag_text:
Regulation Number: 150
Regulation Title: Permission for workings approaching within 60 meters of water/liquid accumulation
Chapter: XI
Clause Number: other
Requirement Type: safety
Requirement: No working which has approached within 60 meters of any other working containing or likely to contain accumulation of water or liquid matter shall be extended further without prior written permission of Chief Inspector.
Responsible Role: Manager, Owner, Agent
Responsible Entity: Mine Management/Owner
Applicability: Workings approaching within 60m of water accumulation
Trigger Event: Working face reaching within 60m of unexamined/water-logged working
Frequency: pre_operation
Deadline: not_specified
Reporting Required: True
Reporting Method: application_or_approval
Reporting Authority: chief_inspector
Document Required: Written permission from Chief Inspector and scheme of working
Record Required: Permission letter and statutory plan/section
Required Evidence: Prior written permission from Chief Inspector
Inspection Required: Yes
Inspection Frequency: Continuous during advance
Equipment Requirement: Not specified
Hazard: Underground inundation, sudden water outburst
Risk Category: CRITICAL
Corrective Action: Stop working face immediately at 60m distance and obtain written permission
Violation Condition: Advancing workings within 60m of water-logged area without Chief Inspector permission
Project Relevance: HIGH
Relevance Reason: Primary safety rule preventing underground inundation disasters.

regulation_title: Action upon observing abnormal water seepage
rag_text:
Regulation Number: 150
Regulation Title: Action upon observing abnormal water seepage
Chapter: XI
Clause Number: other
Requirement Type: emergency
Requirement: Whenever abnormal seepage of water is noticed or suspected, working shall be immediately stopped and Chief Inspector and Regional Inspector informed. Working shall not extend without written permission.
Responsible Role: Manager, Competent Person
Responsible Entity: Mine Management/Owner
Applicability: Any working face displaying abnormal water seepage
Trigger Event: Observation or suspicion of abnormal water seepage
Frequency: immediate
Deadline: immediate
Reporting Required: True
Reporting Method: immediate_notification
Reporting Authority: chief_and_regional_inspector
Document Required: Seepage report and permission application
Record Required: Shift log entry detailing seepage stoppage
Required Evidence: Work stoppage proof and immediate statutory notice sent
Inspection Required: Yes
Inspection Frequency: Immediate emergency inspection
Equipment Requirement: Not specified
Hazard: Impending inundation / water outburst
Risk Category: CRITICAL
Corrective Action: Stop working face immediately, inform CI and RI, await permission
Violation Condition: Continuing work after noticing abnormal water seepage without informing inspectors
Project Relevance: HIGH
Relevance Reason: Critical emergency protocol for inundation warning signs.

regulation_title: Dimensions and exploratory bore-holes in approaching workings
rag_text:
Regulation Number: 150
Regulation Title: Dimensions and exploratory bore-holes in approaching workings
Chapter: XI
Clause Number: multiple_clauses
Requirement Type: safety
Requirement: Height and width of working approaching water shall not exceed 2.4 meters. Center bore-hole and flank bore-holes (at intervals <= 5m) shall be maintained at advance distance >= 3 meters under direct supervision of certified official.
Responsible Role: Manager, Overman
Responsible Entity: Mine Management/Owner
Applicability: Workings extended under sub-reg (3) or (6)
Trigger Event: Advancing working near suspected water body
Frequency: continuous
Deadline: not_specified
Reporting Required: False
Reporting Method: not_specified
Reporting Authority: not_specified
Document Required: Not specified
Record Required: Daily borehole logbook signed by Overman/Manager
Required Evidence: Face dimensions <= 2.4m, flank boreholes <= 5m spacing, advance distance >= 3m
Inspection Required: Yes
Inspection Frequency: Daily direct supervision
Equipment Requirement: Long-hole drilling equipment
Hazard: Accidental holing into water-bearing strata/workings
Risk Category: CRITICAL
Corrective Action: Reduce gallery dimensions to <= 2.4m and drill required flank boreholes ahead
Violation Condition: Gallery width/height > 2.4m, advance distance < 3m, or lack of direct certified supervision
Project Relevance: HIGH
Relevance Reason: Quantitative engineering safe-guards during probe drilling.

regulation_title: Notice of intentional flooding of mine workings
rag_text:
Regulation Number: 151
Regulation Title: Notice of intentional flooding of mine workings
Chapter: XI
Clause Number: other
Requirement Type: reporting
Requirement: When owner, agent or manager intends to flood any part of mine workings, written notice of at least 14 days shall be given to Chief Inspector, Regional Inspector, and management of adjoining mines.
Responsible Role: Owner, Agent, Manager
Responsible Entity: Mine Management/Owner
Applicability: Intentional flooding of mine workings
Trigger Event: Proposal to introduce water to flood workings
Frequency: pre_operation
Deadline: before_event
Reporting Required: True
Reporting Method: written_notification
Reporting Authority: chief_and_regional_inspector
Document Required: Notice of Intentional Flooding
Record Required: Copy of notice and delivery receipts
Required Evidence: Written notice submitted 14 days in advance to authorities and neighbors
Inspection Required: Yes
Inspection Frequency: Prior permission inspection
Equipment Requirement: Not specified
Hazard: Uncontrolled water transfer endangering adjoining mine safety
Risk Category: CRITICAL
Corrective Action: Issue 14 days notice to authorities and adjoining mines before commencing flooding
Violation Condition: Commencing intentional flooding without giving 14 days written notice
Project Relevance: HIGH
Relevance Reason: Statutory notification for major inter-mine safety hazard.

regulation_title: Construction of reservoir, water dam, or retaining structure
rag_text:
Regulation Number: 152
Regulation Title: Construction of reservoir, water dam, or retaining structure
Chapter: XI
Clause Number: other
Requirement Type: reporting
Requirement: Owner, agent or manager shall give at least 14 days written notice accompanied by 2 copies of design plans/sections to Regional Inspector before constructing any reservoir, dam or structure to withstand water pressure.
Responsible Role: Owner, Agent, Manager
Responsible Entity: Mine Management/Owner
Applicability: Construction of water dams/reservoirs underground or surface
Trigger Event: Proposal to construct water dam/reservoir
Frequency: pre_operation
Deadline: before_deadline
Reporting Required: True
Reporting Method: plan_submission
Reporting Authority: regional_inspector
Document Required: Water Dam Design Plans and Sections (2 copies)
Record Required: Approved design plans and construction log
Required Evidence: Notice and plans submitted 14 days prior to construction
Inspection Required: Yes
Inspection Frequency: Pre-construction engineering review
Equipment Requirement: Water retention dam/reservoir structure
Hazard: Dam burst / water dam failure causing catastrophic underground flooding
Risk Category: CRITICAL
Corrective Action: Submit design plans and 14 days notice to Regional Inspector before building
Violation Condition: Constructing water retention dam without 14 days notice or design plans submission
Project Relevance: HIGH
Relevance Reason: Engineering compliance and statutory approval requirement for dams.

regulation_title: Standard of ventilation - Minimum air volume per person and output
rag_text:
Regulation Number: 153
Regulation Title: Standard of ventilation - Minimum air volume per person and output
Chapter: XII
Clause Number: other
Requirement Type: threshold
Requirement: In every ventilating district, not less than 6 m3/min of air per person on largest shift OR not less than 2.5 m3/min per tonne of daily output (whichever is larger) must pass along the last ventilation connection.
Responsible Role: Manager, Ventilation Officer, Owner, Agent
Responsible Entity: Mine Management/Owner
Applicability: Every ventilating district in belowground mine
Trigger Event: Continuous ventilation operation
Frequency: continuous
Deadline: not_specified
Reporting Required: False
Reporting Method: not_specified
Reporting Authority: not_specified
Document Required: Not specified
Record Required: Air measurement book
Required Evidence: Anemometer measurements meeting >= 6 m3/min/person or >= 2.5 m3/min/tonne standard
Inspection Required: Yes
Inspection Frequency: Fortnightly measurement
Equipment Requirement: Mechanical ventilator, anemometer
Hazard: Suffocation, gas accumulation, heat exhaustion underground
Risk Category: HIGH
Corrective Action: Adjust main/booster fan or regulation stoppings to increase airflow
Violation Condition: Airflow at last ventilation connection less than 6 m3/min/person or 2.5 m3/min/tonne
Project Relevance: HIGH
Relevance Reason: Primary numerical threshold for underground mine ventilation.

regulation_title: Standard of ventilation - Air purity and gas concentration limits
rag_text:
Regulation Number: 153
Regulation Title: Standard of ventilation - Air purity and gas concentration limits
Chapter: XII
Clause Number: other
Requirement Type: threshold
Requirement: Air shall contain >= 19% oxygen, <= 0.5% carbon dioxide. Inflammable gas shall not exceed 0.75% in general body of return air of any district, and <= 1.25% in any place in the mine.
Responsible Role: Manager, Ventilation Officer
Responsible Entity: Mine Management/Owner
Applicability: All belowground workplaces and airways
Trigger Event: Air quality monitoring
Frequency: continuous
Deadline: not_specified
Reporting Required: False
Reporting Method: not_specified
Reporting Authority: not_specified
Document Required: Not specified
Record Required: Air sampling and gas analysis book
Required Evidence: Air analysis reports showing O2 >= 19%, CO2 <= 0.5%, CH4 <= 0.75% (return) / 1.25% (any place)
Inspection Required: Yes
Inspection Frequency: At least once every 30 days
Equipment Requirement: Gas detectors, methanometers, air sampling kits
Hazard: Asphyxiation, gas explosion, toxic gas poisoning
Risk Category: CRITICAL
Corrective Action: Enhance ventilation, withdraw persons if CH4 > 1.25% or O2 < 19%
Violation Condition: Oxygen < 19%, CO2 > 0.5%, return CH4 > 0.75%, or CH4 > 1.25% anywhere
Project Relevance: HIGH
Relevance Reason: Core life-safety thresholds for mine gas control.

regulation_title: Standard of ventilation - Temperature and air velocity limits
rag_text:
Regulation Number: 153
Regulation Title: Standard of ventilation - Temperature and air velocity limits
Chapter: XII
Clause Number: other
Requirement Type: threshold
Requirement: Wet bulb temperature in any working place shall not exceed 33.5°C. Where wet bulb temperature exceeds 30.5°C, air current velocity must be at least 1.0 meter per second.
Responsible Role: Manager, Ventilation Officer
Responsible Entity: Mine Management/Owner
Applicability: All belowground working places
Trigger Event: Temperature measurement
Frequency: monthly
Deadline: not_specified
Reporting Required: False
Reporting Method: not_specified
Reporting Authority: not_specified
Document Required: Not specified
Record Required: Temperature reading logbook
Required Evidence: Wet bulb reading <= 33.5°C, and airflow >= 1 m/s when wet bulb > 30.5°C
Inspection Required: Yes
Inspection Frequency: At least once every 30 days
Equipment Requirement: Hygrometer / psychrometer, anemometer
Hazard: Heat stroke, heat exhaustion, severe thermal stress
Risk Category: HIGH
Corrective Action: Increase air velocity above 1 m/s or cool workings if wet bulb > 30.5°C; cease work if > 33.5°C
Violation Condition: Wet bulb temp > 33.5°C, or wet bulb > 30.5°C with air speed < 1 m/s
Project Relevance: HIGH
Relevance Reason: Thermal safety threshold for mine work environment.

regulation_title: Main mechanical ventilator specifications and installation
rag_text:
Regulation Number: 154
Regulation Title: Main mechanical ventilator specifications and installation
Chapter: XII
Clause Number: clause_range
Requirement Type: equipment
Requirement: Main mechanical ventilator must be installed on surface >= 10m from shaft/incline opening, powered by separate electrical circuit from main distribution, have 2 power sources, continuous pressure recorder, air reversal capability, and air lock at shaft.
Responsible Role: Manager, Engineer, Owner, Agent
Responsible Entity: Mine Management/Owner
Applicability: Main mechanical ventilators in belowground mines
Trigger Event: Installation and operation of main fan
Frequency: continuous
Deadline: not_specified
Reporting Required: False
Reporting Method: not_specified
Reporting Authority: not_specified
Document Required: Ventilator installation approval and engineering plans
Record Required: Continuous pressure recording charts, fan maintenance register
Required Evidence: Surface fan >= 10m away, dual power source, pressure recording chart, air lock present
Inspection Required: Yes
Inspection Frequency: Weekly inspection
Equipment Requirement: Main mechanical ventilator, pressure recorder, air lock, dual power supply
Hazard: Total ventilation failure, mine explosion, air reversal failure
Risk Category: CRITICAL
Corrective Action: Provide dual power supply, continuous pressure recorder, and air reversal mechanism
Violation Condition: Single power source, lack of pressure recorder, main fan <10m from shaft (post-1957)
Project Relevance: HIGH
Relevance Reason: Core mechanical infrastructure standard for underground ventilation.

regulation_title: Restriction on installation of booster fan belowground
rag_text:
Regulation Number: 155
Regulation Title: Restriction on installation of booster fan belowground
Chapter: XII
Clause Number: other
Requirement Type: governance
Requirement: In fiery or 2nd/3rd degree gassy seam, no booster fan shall be installed belowground unless manager conducts ventilation survey and sends 7 days prior written notice with survey details to Regional Inspector.
Responsible Role: Manager
Responsible Entity: Mine Management/Owner
Applicability: Fiery seams and 2nd/3rd degree gassy seams
Trigger Event: Proposal to install or shift a booster fan underground
Frequency: weekly
Deadline: before_deadline
Reporting Required: True
Reporting Method: written_notification
Reporting Authority: regional_inspector
Document Required: Ventilation survey report and 7-day prior notice
Record Required: Survey report and notice receipt log
Required Evidence: Written notice submitted to Regional Inspector 7 days prior to booster fan setup
Inspection Required: Yes
Inspection Frequency: Pre-commissioning review
Equipment Requirement: Booster fan
Hazard: Uncontrolled gas recirculation, local explosive gas accumulation
Risk Category: CRITICAL
Corrective Action: Conduct ventilation survey and submit 7 days notice to Regional Inspector
Violation Condition: Installing or shifting a booster fan underground without 7 days prior notice to RI
Project Relevance: HIGH
Relevance Reason: Strict approval rule for underground booster fan deployment.

regulation_title: Supervision, examination, and stoppage logging of mechanical ventilators
rag_text:
Regulation Number: 156
Regulation Title: Supervision, examination, and stoppage logging of mechanical ventilators
Chapter: XII
Clause Number: clause_range
Requirement Type: inspection
Requirement: A competent person shall inspect main ventilator and booster fan weekly, log results in bound paged book, report serious defects to manager immediately. Stoppages must be immediately recorded and signed by manager.
Responsible Role: Competent Person, Manager
Responsible Entity: Mine Management/Owner
Applicability: All mechanical ventilators and booster fans
Trigger Event: Weekly inspection or fan stoppage event
Frequency: immediate
Deadline: immediate
Reporting Required: True
Reporting Method: immediate_notification
Reporting Authority: mine_manager
Document Required: Bound-paged Ventilator Inspection Register
Record Required: Signed weekly examination entries and fan stoppage log
Required Evidence: Competent person report in bound book and manager signature on stoppage entries
Inspection Required: Yes
Inspection Frequency: Every 7 days
Equipment Requirement: Mechanical ventilator, booster fan
Hazard: Ventilation interruption leading to gas buildup underground
Risk Category: CRITICAL
Corrective Action: Log stoppage immediately, notify manager, take corrective safety measures
Violation Condition: Failure to inspect fans weekly or failure to record fan stoppage immediately in bound book
Project Relevance: HIGH
Relevance Reason: Essential operational monitoring protocol for main ventilation assets.

Regulation Number: 156
Regulation Title: Periodic air quantity measurement
Chapter: XII
Clause Number: other
Requirement Type: monitoring
Requirement: In mines with mechanical ventilator, air quantity shall be measured at least once every 14 days in main intake/return, splits, and ventilating districts, and entered in a bound paged book (30 days for non-fiery / 1st degree gassy seams).
Responsible Role: Ventilation Officer, Competent Person, Manager
Responsible Entity: Mine Management/Owner
Applicability: All mines with mechanical ventilators
Trigger Event: Routine air measurement schedule
Frequency: monthly
Deadline: not_specified
Reporting Required: False
Reporting Method: not_specified
Reporting Authority: not_specified
Document Required: Bound paged Air Measurement Book
Record Required: Air measurement records signed by competent person
Required Evidence: Signed entries of airflow volume measurements in bound book
Inspection Required: Yes
Inspection Frequency: Every 14 or 30 days
Equipment Requirement: Anemometer / velometer
Hazard: Undetected drop in air volume causing toxic/flammable gas concentration
Risk Category: HIGH
Corrective Action: Measure air quantities across all splits and record in bound book
Violation Condition: Failure to measure air quantity within 14 days (or 30 days in 1st degree)
Project Relevance: HIGH
Relevance Reason: Statutory monitoring schedule for ventilation distribution.

Regulation Number: 157
Regulation Title: Standing orders for ventilator stoppage
Chapter: XII
Clause Number: clause_range
Requirement Type: governance
Requirement: Manager shall submit standing orders for withdrawal of persons during ventilator stoppage to Regional Inspector within 30 days of installation, and display approved copies in English and local language.
Responsible Role: Manager
Responsible Entity: Mine Management/Owner
Applicability: Mines with mechanical ventilators (other than auxiliary fans)
Trigger Event: Installation of main/booster mechanical ventilator
Frequency: monthly
Deadline: other
Reporting Required: True
Reporting Method: application_or_approval
Reporting Authority: regional_inspector
Document Required: Standing Orders for Fan Stoppage
Record Required: Approved standing orders and display verification
Required Evidence: Regional Inspector approval letter and displayed notices in English and local language
Inspection Required: Yes
Inspection Frequency: Periodic audit
Equipment Requirement: Notice boards for standing orders
Hazard: Panic or failure to evacuate during main fan failure
Risk Category: HIGH
Corrective Action: Submit standing orders within 30 days and post conspicuous bilingual notices
Violation Condition: Failure to submit standing orders within 30 days or lack of displayed bilingual copies
Project Relevance: HIGH
Relevance Reason: Emergency compliance rule for fan outage events.

regulation_title: Independent intake airways for ventilating districts
rag_text:
Regulation Number: 158
Regulation Title: Independent intake airways for ventilating districts
Chapter: XII
Clause Number: other
Requirement Type: safety
Requirement: In every ventilating district there shall be provided two independent intake airways, one of which shall be used as a travelling roadway, unless exempted by Regional Inspector.
Responsible Role: Manager, Owner, Agent
Responsible Entity: Mine Management/Owner
Applicability: Every ventilating district in belowground mine
Trigger Event: District ventilation design and development
Frequency: continuous
Deadline: not_specified
Reporting Required: True
Reporting Method: application_or_approval
Reporting Authority: regional_inspector
Document Required: Exemption order from RI if less than 2 intakes provided
Record Required: Ventilation plan showing 2 independent intakes
Required Evidence: Two independent intake airways shown on plan and physically verified
Inspection Required: Yes
Inspection Frequency: Periodic inspection
Equipment Requirement: Not specified
Hazard: Trapping of personnel due to blockage of single intake/travelling roadway
Risk Category: CRITICAL
Corrective Action: Provide second independent intake airway or seek RI exemption
Violation Condition: Operating a ventilating district with only one intake airway without RI exemption
Project Relevance: HIGH
Relevance Reason: Crucial structural escape and ventilation redundancy requirement.

Regulation Number: 159
Regulation Title: Construction thickness of ventilation stoppings
Chapter: XII
Clause Number: other
Requirement Type: safety
Requirement: Every stopping between main intake and main return airways shall be constructed of masonry/brickwork/unreinforced concrete not less than 25cm thick (or reinforced concrete >= 15cm thick), faced with lime/cement plaster to prevent leakage.
Responsible Role: Manager, Owner, Agent
Responsible Entity: Mine Management/Owner
Applicability: Stoppings between main intake and return airways
Trigger Event: Erection of ventilation stoppings
Frequency: continuous
Deadline: not_specified
Reporting Required: False
Reporting Method: not_specified
Reporting Authority: not_specified
Document Required: Not specified
Record Required: Stopping construction log
Required Evidence: Masonry thickness >= 25cm or RCC >= 15cm with plaster coat
Inspection Required: Yes
Inspection Frequency: Every 14 days
Equipment Requirement: Masonry, reinforced concrete, plastering
Hazard: Short-circuiting of intake air into return airway
Risk Category: HIGH
Corrective Action: Rebuild stopping to mandatory thickness (>=25cm masonry / >=15cm RCC) and plaster
Violation Condition: Stopping thickness less than 25cm (masonry) or 15cm (RCC) or unplastered surface
Project Relevance: HIGH
Relevance Reason: Engineering specifications for main ventilation control structures.

Regulation Number: 159
Regulation Title: Periodic examination of ventilation appliances
Chapter: XII
Clause Number: other
Requirement Type: inspection
Requirement: A competent person shall, once at least in every 14 days, examine every airway, air crossing, ventilation stopping and door in use, and record the result in a bound paged book.
Responsible Role: Competent Person
Responsible Entity: Mine Management/Owner
Applicability: All belowground ventilation appliances and airways
Trigger Event: Routine inspection schedule
Frequency: periodic
Deadline: not_specified
Reporting Required: False
Reporting Method: not_specified
Reporting Authority: not_specified
Document Required: Bound paged Ventilation Examination Book
Record Required: Signed inspection reports of airways and ventilation devices
Required Evidence: Signed and dated inspection entries in bound paged book
Inspection Required: Yes
Inspection Frequency: Every 14 days
Equipment Requirement: Not specified
Hazard: Damaged doors, broken stoppings causing ventilation collapse
Risk Category: HIGH
Corrective Action: Conduct immediate inspection and repair damaged ventilation devices
Violation Condition: Failure to examine airways and ventilation devices every 14 days
Project Relevance: HIGH
Relevance Reason: Regular maintenance inspection mandate for ventilation network.

Regulation Number: 160
Regulation Title: Minimum velocity of air current
Chapter: XII
Clause Number: other
Requirement Type: threshold
Requirement: Air velocity (m/min) shall meet Table limits: Immediate outbye connection (30 m/min); 4.5m from face (30 for 1st/2nd degree, 45 for 3rd degree); 7.5m from air pipe discharge (15 for 1st/2nd, 25 for 3rd); longwall max span (60 for 1st/2nd, 75 for 3rd).
Responsible Role: Manager, Ventilation Officer
Responsible Entity: Mine Management/Owner
Applicability: All working faces, longwall faces, and air pipe discharges
Trigger Event: Air current velocity measurement
Frequency: periodic
Deadline: not_specified
Reporting Required: False
Reporting Method: not_specified
Reporting Authority: not_specified
Document Required: Not specified
Record Required: Air velocity measurement register
Required Evidence: Anemometer readings complying with statutory Table values
Inspection Required: Yes
Inspection Frequency: Every 14 days
Equipment Requirement: Anemometer, velometer
Hazard: Gas layering, stagnant air, gas accumulation at working faces
Risk Category: CRITICAL
Corrective Action: Adjust auxiliary fans or brattice to achieve statutory minimum air velocity
Violation Condition: Air velocity below specified Table values at designated face points
Project Relevance: HIGH
Relevance Reason: Numerical air speed thresholds for mine gas dilution.

regulation_title: Auxiliary fan installation, earthing, and ducting standards
rag_text:
Regulation Number: 161
Regulation Title: Auxiliary fan installation, earthing, and ducting standards
Chapter: XII
Clause Number: other
Requirement Type: equipment
Requirement: Auxiliary fans shall prevent re-circulation of air, be efficiently earthed to prevent electrostatic charge accumulation, and have air-ducts delivering/exhausting air to within 3.0 meters of face or blind end.
Responsible Role: Manager, Engineer, Competent Person
Responsible Entity: Mine Management/Owner
Applicability: All auxiliary fan installations belowground
Trigger Event: Installation and operation of auxiliary fans
Frequency: continuous
Deadline: not_specified
Reporting Required: False
Reporting Method: not_specified
Reporting Authority: not_specified
Document Required: Not specified
Record Required: Auxiliary fan inspection log
Required Evidence: Air duct extended to within 3m of face, earthing ground test compliance
Inspection Required: Yes
Inspection Frequency: Daily supervision / Weekly check
Equipment Requirement: Auxiliary fan, flexible/rigid ventilation air duct, earthing connection
Hazard: Gas re-circulation, electrostatic spark ignition, gas buildup at face
Risk Category: CRITICAL
Corrective Action: Extend air duct to within 3.0m of face and connect earth conductor
Violation Condition: Air duct ending more than 3.0m from face, fan re-circulating air, or missing earthing
Project Relevance: HIGH
Relevance Reason: Crucial technical requirement for face ventilation and spark safety.

regulation_title: Precautions against fire in ventilation appliances
rag_text:
Regulation Number: 162
Regulation Title: Precautions against fire in ventilation appliances
Chapter: XII
Clause Number: multiple_clauses
Requirement Type: safety
Requirement: Main mechanical ventilator on surface shall be installed in a fireproof housing. Belowground fans (other than auxiliary) shall have exposed coal/carbonaceous material on roof, sides and floor covered with fire-resistant masonry or coating.
Responsible Role: Manager, Owner, Agent
Responsible Entity: Mine Management/Owner
Applicability: Surface main ventilators and underground booster/main fans
Trigger Event: Installation of mechanical ventilation housing
Frequency: continuous
Deadline: not_specified
Reporting Required: False
Reporting Method: not_specified
Reporting Authority: not_specified
Document Required: Fireproof construction specifications
Record Required: Not specified
Required Evidence: Fireproof surface fan building and masonry/fireproof lining around underground fan
Inspection Required: Yes
Inspection Frequency: Periodic audit
Equipment Requirement: Fireproof housing structure, masonry coating
Hazard: Fan housing fire causing catastrophic disruption to mine air supply
Risk Category: CRITICAL
Corrective Action: Construct fireproof housing on surface and line underground fan drift with masonry
Violation Condition: Surface ventilator in non-fireproof structure or exposed coal around underground fan
Project Relevance: HIGH
Relevance Reason: Fire protection requirement for critical ventilation machinery.

regulation_title: Ventilation plans to be brought up-to-date
rag_text:
Regulation Number: 162
Regulation Title: Ventilation plans to be brought up-to-date
Chapter: CHAPTER XII - VENTILATION
Clause Number: other
Requirement Type: safety
Requirement: The covering of every shaft sealed off or covered for ventilation purposes, every fan drift, duct or casing and every part of a mechanical ventilator or fan within such drift, duct or casing, and every air-crossing and ventilation door shall be constructed of fire-proof material.
Responsible Role: 
Responsible Entity: Mine Management/Owner
Applicability: All belowground mines
Trigger Event: Installation or construction of shaft covering, fan drift, duct, casing, air-crossing, or ventilation door
Frequency: continuous
Deadline: not_specified
Reporting Required: False
Reporting Method: not_specified
Reporting Authority: not_specified
Document Required: Not specified
Record Required: Not specified
Required Evidence: Not specified
Inspection Required: Yes
Inspection Frequency: Periodic
Equipment Requirement: Fire-proof material construction for shaft coverings, fan drifts, ducts, casings, air-crossings, and ventilation doors
Hazard: Mine fire
Risk Category: HIGH
Corrective Action: Not specified
Violation Condition: Use of non-fireproof material in ventilation structures or shaft coverings.
Project Relevance: HIGH
Relevance Reason: Mandates fire-proof construction for ventilation infrastructure belowground.

regulation_title: Ventilation plans to be brought up-to-date
rag_text:
Regulation Number: 163
Regulation Title: Ventilation plans to be brought up-to-date
Chapter: CHAPTER XII - VENTILATION
Clause Number: other
Requirement Type: reporting
Requirement: The manager shall ensure that as soon as any alteration is made in the ventilation of a mine involving the erection or removal of an air-crossing or stopping or the alteration in the position or installation of a ventilator or fan belowground, the alteration is notified to the surveyor, who shall forthwith make necessary alterations on the ventilation plan.
Responsible Role: manager, surveyor
Responsible Entity: Mine Management/Owner
Applicability: All belowground mines
Trigger Event: Alteration in ventilation involving erection/removal of air-crossing, stopping, or fan position
Frequency: event_based
Deadline: immediate
Reporting Required: True
Reporting Method: other
Reporting Authority: surveyor
Document Required: Ventilation plan maintained under regulation 65
Record Required: Updated ventilation plan
Required Evidence: Updated ventilation plan with recorded date of alteration
Inspection Required: No
Inspection Frequency: Not specified
Equipment Requirement: Not specified
Hazard: Inaccurate ventilation mapping leading to explosion or asphyxiation risk
Risk Category: MEDIUM
Corrective Action: Update ventilation plan immediately upon ventilation structure changes.
Violation Condition: Failure to notify surveyor or failure of surveyor to update ventilation plan forthwith after alterations.
Project Relevance: HIGH
Relevance Reason: Critical administrative compliance requirement for ventilation tracking.

Regulation Number: 164
Regulation Title: Obstructions, interruptions and alterations
Chapter: CHAPTER XII - VENTILATION
Clause Number: other
Requirement Type: operational
Requirement: No material or debris shall be allowed to accumulate in any level, drive, crosscut, roadway or any other part of the workings belowground so as to impede the ventilation.

Responsible Entity: Mine Management/Owner

Frequency: continuous
Deadline: not_specified
Reporting Required: False
Reporting Method: not_specified
Reporting Authority: not_specified
Document Required: Not specified
Record Required: Not specified
Required Evidence: Clear roadways and airways
Inspection Required: Yes
Inspection Frequency: Daily
Equipment Requirement: Not specified
Hazard: Ventilation blockage leading to accumulation of toxic or inflammable gas
Risk Category: HIGH
Corrective Action: Clear debris and material obstructing airways immediately.
Violation Condition: Accumulation of debris impeding mine airflow.
Project Relevance: HIGH
Relevance Reason: Direct impact on mine safety and air distribution.

Regulation Number: 164
Regulation Title: Obstructions, interruptions and alterations
Chapter: CHAPTER XII - VENTILATION
Clause Number: other
Requirement Type: safety
Requirement: Every roadway and working belowground which is not adequately ventilated shall be fenced or barricaded so as to effectively prevent persons entering the same.
Responsible Role: manager, competent person
Responsible Entity: Mine Management/Owner

Frequency: immediate
Deadline: immediate
Reporting Required: False
Reporting Method: not_specified
Reporting Authority: not_specified
Document Required: Not specified
Record Required: Not specified
Required Evidence: Fencing or barricading across unventilated entry points
Inspection Required: Yes
Inspection Frequency: Continuous monitoring
Equipment Requirement: Fencing/barricading structures
Hazard: Asphyxiation or gas explosion in unventilated areas
Risk Category: HIGH
Corrective Action: Erect effective fence or barricade to restrict access.
Violation Condition: Failure to fence or barricade inadequately ventilated workings.
Project Relevance: HIGH
Relevance Reason: Essential physical safety barrier to prevent unauthorized entry into unventilated zones.

regulation_title: Precautions against gas during de-watering and re-opening
rag_text:
Regulation Number: 165
Regulation Title: Precautions against gas during de-watering and re-opening
Chapter: CHAPTER XII - VENTILATION
Clause Number: other
Requirement Type: safety
Requirement: No disused mine or shaft shall be de-watered except under the constant supervision of a competent person and during such de-watering, approved safety lamps or torches shall be exclusively used, and there shall also be kept burning at every place where persons are at work, at least one approved flame safety lamp.

Trigger Event: De-watering operations
Frequency: continuous
Deadline: not_specified

Reporting Authority: not_specified
Document Required: Not specified
Record Required: Not specified
Required Evidence: Supervision logs, presence of flame safety lamps
Inspection Required: Yes
Inspection Frequency: Constant supervision
Equipment Requirement: Approved safety lamps or torches, approved flame safety lamp
Hazard: Accidental release of noxious/inflammable gas or oxygen deficiency during dewatering
Risk Category: HIGH
Corrective Action: Cease de-watering until competent supervision and approved safety lamps are present.
Violation Condition: De-watering without constant competent supervision or without approved flame safety lamps burning at work sites.
Project Relevance: HIGH
Relevance Reason: High-risk operational protocol during de-watering.

regulation_title: Precautions against gas during de-watering and re-opening
rag_text:
Regulation Number: 165
Regulation Title: Precautions against gas during de-watering and re-opening
Chapter: CHAPTER XII - VENTILATION
Clause Number: other
Requirement Type: inspection
Requirement: The first inspection of a mine or part which is re-opened after discontinuance of mining operations for a period exceeding seven days and of any part of a mine after being de-watered, shall be made by a competent person with an approved flame safety lamp or other approved apparatus for determining presence of inflammable or noxious gases and deficiency of oxygen and during such inspection, no additional light or lamp other than an approved electric torch or lamp shall be used.
Responsible Role: competent person
Responsible Entity: Mine Management/Owner
Applicability: Re-opening mine/part discontinued >7 days, or post de-watering

Deadline: before_event
Reporting Required: False
Reporting Method: not_specified
Reporting Authority: not_specified
Document Required: Not specified
Record Required: Inspection report in bound paged book
Required Evidence: Signed inspection entry in bound paged book
Inspection Required: Yes
Inspection Frequency: Prior to resumption
Equipment Requirement: Approved flame safety lamp or approved gas/oxygen detection apparatus, approved electric torch/lamp
Hazard: Exposure to accumulated hazardous gas or oxygen-deficient atmosphere
Risk Category: HIGH

regulation_title: Precautions against inflammable and noxious gases
rag_text:
Regulation Number: 166
Regulation Title: Precautions against inflammable and noxious gases

Relevance Reason: Defines statutory detection threshold for Degree 1 gassy mines.

regulation_title: Precautions against inflammable and noxious gases
rag_text:
Regulation Number: 166

All persons shall be withdrawn from the place, the place immediately fenced off to prevent inadvertent entry, and the competent person in charge shall without delay take steps to remove gas by improving ventilation.

Required Evidence: Incident report in bound paged book, fencing erection
Inspection Required: Yes

Equipment Requirement: Fencing material
Hazard: Inflammable / toxic gas explosion or poisoning
Risk Category: HIGH
Corrective Action: Evacuate area, erect fencing, increase ventilation airflow.

Relevance Reason: Core life safety procedure during emergency gas detection.

Clause Number: other

regulation_title: Determination of percentage of inflammable gas and of environmental conditions
rag_text:
Regulation Number: 169
Regulation Title: Determination of percentage of inflammable gas and of environmental conditions
Chapter: CHAPTER XII - VENTILATION
Clause Number: other
Requirement Type: emergency
Requirement: If any determination in any ventilating district shows the percentage of inflammable gas to exceed 1.25%, the supply of electric energy shall be cut off immediately from all cables and apparatus in the district, and a written report submitted to the Regional Inspector forthwith.
Responsible Role: competent person, manager, electrical official
Responsible Entity: Mine Management/Owner
Applicability: Ventilating districts using electric energy belowground

Frequency: immediate
Deadline: immediate

Reporting Method: immediate_notification
Reporting Authority: regional_inspector

Record Required: Bound book record and formal report to Regional Inspector
Required Evidence: Power trip log, copy of written report sent to Regional Inspector
Inspection Required: Yes
Inspection Frequency: Continuous gas monitoring
Equipment Requirement: Automatic or manual power isolation apparatus, approved gas monitor
Hazard: Electrical spark ignition of methane gas
Risk Category: HIGH
Corrective Action: Cut off power immediately and notify Regional Inspector in writing.
Violation Condition: Failure to cut off electrical power when gas exceeds 1.25% or failure to report to Regional Inspector forthwith.
Project Relevance: HIGH
Relevance Reason: Critical electrical isolation and emergency reporting rule triggered by methane percentage.

Regulation Number: 171
Regulation Title: General precautions in gassy mines
Chapter: CHAPTER XII - VENTILATION
Clause Number: other
Requirement Type: operational
Requirement: No working or gallery shall be extended to a distance of more than 3 meters from the nearest ventilation connection unless the current of air is coursed up to a point within 3 meters of the face by means of fire resistant pipes, tubes, brattices or other material.
Responsible Role: manager, overman, sirdar
Responsible Entity: Mine Management/Owner
Applicability: All gassy coal mines

Frequency: continuous
Deadline: not_specified

Reporting Authority: not_specified

Record Required: Not specified

Inspection Required: Yes

Equipment Requirement: Fire resistant pipes, tubes, or brattices
Hazard: Stagnant air and gas accumulation at working face
Risk Category: HIGH

Violation Condition: Extending gallery >3 meters without air coursing within 3 meters of face using fire-resistant materials.

Relevance Reason: Specific numerical physical ventilation requirement at working faces.

Regulation Number: 172
Regulation Title: Contrabands

Clause Number: other

Requirement: No person shall have in his possession belowground in a mine any cigar, cigarette, biri, or other smoking apparatus, or any match or mobile phone or other apparatus of any kind capable of producing a light, flame or spark. A competent person shall search every person immediately before entering the mine by turning out pockets, passing hands over clothing, and examining carried articles.

Requirement: Underground relighting stations for safety lamps shall be fixed by the manager at suitable places, legibly marked RELIGHTING STATION, situated in a main intake airway, and placed in charge of a competent person holding a Gas Testing Certificate.
